newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ManFed, Farmers laud RBNZ monetary policy stance.
newsitem.headline: ManFed, Farmers laud RBNZ monetary policy stance.

text.p: Agricultural lobby group Federated Farmers and the New Zealand Manufacturers' Federation on Thursday welcomed the Reserve Bank's easing of monetary conditions.

In its six-montly economic projections released earlier on Thursday, the RBNZ said there was scope for monetary conditions to ease somewhat, which prompted the New Zealand dollar to fall about 30 basis points to US$0.7020, and the 90-day bank bill rate to fall nearly 20 points to 7.38 percent at 12.45 p.m. (2345 GMT).
"Manufacturers will applaud the Reserve Bank's new stance," ManFed said.
"In particular we want the exchange rate to retreat, and we are less concerned at the moment if interest rates remain high to help achieve this."
ManFed said the change in monetary outlook was also welcome in view of New Zealand's worsening balance of payments situation.
"Clearly the Reserve bank is acting to assist a return to export growth and to limit imports to help shore up our current account problem," ManFed said.
Federated Farmers said the Kiwi's fall would provide some relief for farmers but expressed concern at the implications of future government spending.
"The bank's statement shows that the current mix of government spending and the Reserve Bank's efforts to keep low inflation is not working as well as it should," Federated Farmers said.
It said the RBNZ forecasts showed the government's recent spending policies would make a significant contribution to inflation a couple of years out.
"If exporters have to pay the price of that with higher exchange and interest rates then the whole country will be worse off."
Federated Framers also said the high value of the Kiwi was contributing to the worsening balance of payments deficit.
